parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal entry exposure: sex-binary passport rules (X-marker eliminated, ASAB-only issuance upheld Nov 2025), a consular cable directing refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, documented confiscations stranding travelers, and advisories from 8+ foreign governments. Facilities bans reach ~22 units (4 criminalizing in some circumstances), with one documented arrest and 24-hour men's-ward placement. Federal corrections and immigration custody show conversion-style policies and reported abuse. This is tier-1 exposure. Offsetting: no criminalization of trans identity, functioning courts enjoining orders, national employment/hate-crime protections, and 33+ units with no mapped ban. Imprisonment is not likely for an ordinary visitor.

entry_documents.exposure: Jan 2025 order ends self-selected markers; X-marker processing stopped Feb 2025; SCOTUS allowed restriction Nov 2025. Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and directs officers to consider a fraud ground carrying possible lifetime ineligibility. Passports confiscated/blocked; travelers stranded; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers, is never automatic, and no documented imposition as of Nov 2025-2026; litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → secondary screening/refusal → possible detention → birth-sex placement downstream.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented trespass arrest (19 Mar 2025) with 24 hours held in men's ward. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric therapy) and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts in 2025. Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse (single encyclopedic source, uncorroborated).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; national hate-crime statute; active civil-rights litigation; pretrial release granted in the documented case.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy → fraud investigation → custody → birth-sex placement; facility enforcement → arrest → same custody pipeline.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Bans in 9+1 units covering all government buildings, 9 units covering schools plus some government buildings, 3 units schools-only; 6 units extend to some private settings; 4 units criminalize in certain circumstances. One arrest documented. Feb 2026 law in one unit invalidates non-ASAB birth certificates/licences and bars sex-segregated facility use, called a template. 4 units flagged 'Do Not Travel' by one advocacy publication.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units, 4 others and the capital district have no mapped ban; 22 units plus capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination; some full-support state scorecards.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facility ban + national document regime → outed visitor faces both exclusion and, in 4 units, criminal charge.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for minors in 27 units; Oct 2025 proposed rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; Jan 2025 executive order frames such care as 'mutilation'; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut Jul 2025. No documented visitor-specific adult care denial.
care_services.protection: Proposed rules remain proposed; litigation pending; adult emergency care restriction for visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor: entry document regime plus 27-unit care bans sharply limit continuity of care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes identifying and neutralizing groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 cash-reward memo references 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; Jan 2025 order directs law enforcement to investigate schools promoting 'gender ideology'. Official hostility is documented in primary documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states the reward criterion is not 'radical gender ideology' and that CT powers will not target those who merely disagree; no posted reward or enforcement action documented as of Nov 2026.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and severity of any police encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor's passport follows the same ASAB-only regime; 27-unit care bans; Jan 2025 order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; Oct 2025 proposed insurance rule targets under-18 care.
minors_guardians.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined in court; criminal-prosecution order's enforcement against travelers not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent travelling with trans minor: document mismatch at entry plus care denial in many units.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence or killing rate in the dossier, so no comparison to background homicide is possible. 66% poll support for ASAB on government documents; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes and 37 lacked them as of 2019; 4 units criminalize facility use in some circumstances.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment-discrimination ruling remains; 22 units plus capital district bar gender-identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin street-level recourse in non-protective units compounds facility and document exposures.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and multiple executive-order challenges unresolved; implementation of the sex-doubt refusal cable and fraud ground unknown; do-not-travel criteria unstated; no airport-screening data specific to trans travelers; custody-abuse reports single-sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts issuing injunctions; civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs; maintained legal-aid FAQ; national equality and identity-document maps tracking changes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation means exposure fluctuates by travel date, but in-force rules (passport regime, facility bans) govern now.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register produces routine entry exclusion with no remedy. This dossier shares that universal document-based entry exposure but adds criminal facility exposure in 4 units, a documented arrest with men's-ward placement, and reported custody abuse — materially more severe consequences after discovery than exclusion alone.

Kestrel Isles offers discretionary secondary screening ending in administrative refusal with written reasons and appeal. This regime is worse: markers cannot be corrected, refusal is instructed on sex doubt with a possible lifetime bar, and downstream unit-level criminal facility exposure and custody harm exist. Below 0.55.

Drellia's mandatory registration and nightly hotel reporting create continuous exposure with slow, confidential remedies and uncommon criminal charges. Similar structure here (universal document exposure, bureaucratic outing), but this dossier adds criminal facility statutes, documented custody abuse, and stronger judicial pushback than Drellia's ombuds-only remedy.

Meridia trains border officers, accepts congruent markers, and offers tribunal release with compensation. This jurisdiction does the opposite: it mandates ASAB markers, instructs refusal on sex doubt, and its courts have not yet delivered relief on the in-force passport policy. Far below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-stage operative regime. At entry, the federal document regime is universal and in force: markers cannot be made congruent, screening instructions direct refusal on sex doubt, and foreign governments have issued advisories — a tier-1 exposure with litigation pending but no demonstrated remedy yet. Inside, facility bans across roughly 22 units (criminal in 4, with one documented arrest and men's-ward holding) combine with a Feb 2026 document-invalidating law and four do-not-travel units. Custody compounds this: birth-sex placement is documented, and federal custody reports include forced labour and conversion-style policies. Imprisonment is not likely for an ordinary visitor, and courts, hate-crime law, and 33+ unbaned units materially cushion the picture — but the harshest operative rules, not the protections, govern discovery.
